newsitem.title: UK: Poll says British MP in sleaze row should resign.
newsitem.headline: Poll says British MP in sleaze row should resign.

text.p: Most British people believe Neil Hamilton, a former Conservative minister who is the target of sleaze allegations, should resign now, an opinion poll indicated on Tuesday.

Sixty-two percent of voters polled by the Guardian newspaper said former minister should step down and 54 percent said Prime Minister John Major was not being tough enough in dealing with the allegations.

Hamilton, who sensationally dropped a libel case against the Guardian at the last moment, has admitted accepting 10,000 pounds ($15,000) from political lobbyist Ian Greer but denied he took money in return for asking questions in parliament.

Greer announced at the weekend he was resigning as chairman of his lobbying company and immediately gave an interview to the Times in which he said he had raised 750,000 pounds ($1.17 million) for the Conservatives over the past decade.
He also said he was paid to provide a car and offices for the 1990 campaign at which Major won the party leadership and ministers had approached him for help with election expenses.

The latest Guardian poll of voter intentions showed 49 percent of voters backed the opposition Labour Party, 31 percent the Conservatives and 16 percent backed the centrist Liberal Democrats. Others made up the rest.
The prime minister must call a general election by next May.
